title: Condon's band and its Columbia albums
summary: Leeman says the Condon band never had a bad moment, made two Columbia albums including 'Jammin' at Condon's', and alternated with guest house sets.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But that band never had a bad moment in two or three years that I was playing down there off and on. This was downtown -- because I worked for 22 years off and on with Eddie Garner, which we'll get into later. But that band -- Bill and I are the only two people alive out of that one. For people who went there and felt and heard it -- and it was well known at the time -- we made a beautiful thing together. We made two albums for Columbia, I think you know -- they were picked two of the greatest all time jazz records -- Jammin' at Condon's and East Coast West Coast Jazz. (among others) (Enroll)

And we had two bands then, Eddie Condon -- used the house band for one set of a half hour for awhile, and then he'd switch over, and the guests would play, like Bill Butterfield, Bud Freeman -- do you understand what I'm getting at?
Of course, Cliff, I was there, too.
